editions.intro: Two spy stories and a blocked impeachment lead the big newsrooms this morning: the Nvidia affair, the arrest of a US soldier in Britain, and the House vote that spared Pete Hegseth. British outlets are dominated by the David Walliams allegations.

leading.headline: The Woman in the Middle of Nvidia’s Spy Scandal
leading.text: US intelligence has concluded that Alice Huang, who had an affair with Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, is a Chinese asset; the Times also reports Trump had been reminded of the intelligence before his China trip.
leading.ranks: Leads: NYT. Most read No. 1: NYT, WaPo. High on: WaPo, ynet. Also on: BBC.

leading.headline: Hegseth impeachment effort is blocked by House Republicans
leading.text: Republicans shelved impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth that Rep. Thomas Massie, a fellow Republican, had forced to a vote; Democrats can try again next year.
leading.ranks: Leads: WaPo, Guardian (international). Top 5: NYT, BBC. Most read: WaPo No. 2, Guardian No. 2, BBC No. 5, NYT trending No. 5.

leading.headline: David Walliams accused of using celebrity status to prey on young women for sex
leading.text: The Guardian and ITV News published allegations against the British comedian and children’s author after he lost a court bid to stop them; he denies all of them.
leading.ranks: Leads: Guardian (UK), The Times. Most read No. 1: Guardian; three of BBC’s top 4. Also on the NYT homepage.

leading.headline: US Army soldier suspected of spying for Russia arrested in UK
leading.text: British counterterrorism police arrested a 41-year-old senior US soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of national security offenses linked to Russia.
leading.ranks: Top 3: BBC. Top of the news section: Guardian (UK). On the front: The Times, WaPo, Times of Israel.

leading.headline: Three Iran-backed suspects plotted attacks including RAF Fairford incident, US says
leading.text: The US Justice Department charged three men it says are Iran-backed operatives behind a string of plots, including an incident near a British air base used by US forces; the Times of Israel notes alleged attacks on Jews in London and New York.
leading.ranks: Leads: BBC (international). On the front: Guardian (international), The Times, Times of Israel.

leading.headline: Bernie Sanders Opposes Schumer as Majority Leader
leading.text: With Democrats set to run both houses (the NYT tally is 54 Senate seats and 255 House seats), the fights are now over leadership, the Mississippi Senate count and Republicans’ choice of Jim Jordan as House minority leader.
leading.ranks: Several NYT homepage slots; NYT trending No. 3 (Mississippi). WaPo homepage Nos. 2–3 and most read Nos. 3–4. Also on BBC and Times of Israel.

leading.headline: In furious speech demanding ‘unity government,’ Netanyahu claims Arab MKs want Israel’s destruction
leading.text: Israel’s 26th Knesset was sworn in, Netanyahu is now caretaker prime minister, and Gadi Eisenkot’s bloc is moving to form a government.
leading.ranks: Leads: Times of Israel. High on: ynet. Most read No. 5: Guardian. On the front: WaPo, BBC world page.

leading.headline: Federal judge allows Trump’s $10bn defamation lawsuit against BBC to proceed
leading.text: A US judge ruled that Trump’s $10 billion defamation case against the BBC can go ahead.
leading.ranks: Most read No. 3: Guardian. On the front: Guardian (UK and international), BBC, The Times.

israel.para: In Israel, both outlets lead the politics coverage with the new Knesset and the fight over who forms the next government. Abroad, the Guardian’s Knesset story is its fifth most viewed; the Post and the BBC carry it on their world pages; the NYT’s most-read Israel items are opinion pieces. The London Times homepage had no Israel story among the links read.

items.outlet: ynet; also the Times of Israel top line
items.text: Both Israeli outlets put this NYT report high: Scott Bessent left his home after Iranian threats.

items.headline: The hope of blocking a government fades: Netanyahu aims for two years, Eisenkot is losing patience (in Hebrew)
items.text: Netanyahu met the head of United Torah Judaism to keep it out of the change bloc; Eisenkot canceled a negotiating meeting after the speech.

items.text: Other bills include term limits for the prime minister.

items.headline: Israel’s newly elected parliament is already moving against Netanyahu
items.text: On the Post’s homepage, below the US and Nvidia stories.

items.text: Fifth on the Guardian’s most-viewed list; the UK front also carries Gaza families without shelter after storms.

items.text: On the BBC world page; the international homepage also runs the Board of Peace calling Israel’s Gaza flood aid “insufficient.”

items.headline: It’s Time for Israelis to Throw Out Their Trump
items.text: Thomas Friedman’s column is No. 8 on NYT trending; “JD Vance Trots Out an Old Scapegoat,” on Israel and the midterms, is also on the list.

culture.headline: M John Harrison becomes first science fiction author to win the Booker prize
culture.text: The 81-year-old won for The End of Everything, a post-apocalyptic novel, and is the oldest winner ever, the BBC notes.

culture.headline: The Rise of the Gen Z Cinephile
culture.text: Teenagers and people in their 20s are filling US theaters for blockbusters, indie films and classics; it is on NYT trending.

culture.headline: Stacy Keach, Actor Who Embodied Hamlet and Mike Hammer, Dies at 85
culture.text: The stage and screen actor’s obituary is on the NYT homepage.

culture.headline: The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power season three review – this dull show’s revamp is too little, too late
culture.text: The Guardian’s TV critic is unimpressed by the fantasy series’ return; it is on the UK front page.

culture.headline: Paul McCartney becomes a billionaire and world’s third richest musician
culture.text: Forbes puts his net worth at $1.4 billion, behind Jay-Z and Taylor Swift.

culture.headline: One of America’s Most Brilliant New Restaurants Is in the Sonoran Desert
culture.text: A review of Ursa in Tucson, Arizona, where chef Aaron Lopez cooks food of the Southwest.

culture.headline: New Research Compares Long-Term Relief From 21 Antidepressants
culture.text: A large review found a few drugs worked better over time; the BBC’s version, in its UK top five, says three pills, led by escitalopram, beat Prozac at preventing relapse.

culture.headline: The U.S. Has Lost Its Measles-Elimination Status, Data Suggests
culture.text: A health story listed on the NYT trending page.

sports.headline: The Monaco summit that will decide the future of Carrick and Man Utd
sports.text: Manchester United’s leaders meet in Monaco on Wednesday to decide whether coach Michael Carrick stays; it leads BBC Sport and Guardian Sport, and The Athletic revisits Jim Ratcliffe’s promises.

sports.headline: Australia tampered with ball during Ashes, reveals Khawaja
sports.text: Usman Khawaja’s autobiography has reopened Australia’s ball-tampering scandal; it is on the Times homepage and also on BBC Sport and Guardian Sport.

sports.headline: Formula 1 to finish season in Middle East
sports.text: The Qatar and Abu Dhabi races will go ahead as planned, and Italy’s Imola circuit has been stood down as the backup; the Guardian notes safety concerns.

editions.method: Order is each outlet’s own homepage order and most-read lists, read 08:35–08:50 Israel time. NYT from the signed-in homepage and nytimes.com/trending; WaPo and The Times through the r.jina.ai reader; BBC, Guardian and ynet from their public homepages; Times of Israel from its homepage and RSS feed; sections from RSS feeds.
editions.cover: The big newsrooms split on what matters most today. The New York Times leads with the woman at the center of the Nvidia spy scandal, which is also No. 1 on the Times and Washington Post most-read lists. The Post leads with House Republicans blocking the Hegseth impeachment. In Britain, The Guardian and The Times lead with the allegations against David Walliams, which he denies, and the BBC's top stories include the arrest of a US Army soldier near Gloucester on suspicion of spying for Russia. The Times of Israel leads with Netanyahu's Knesset speech. Away from the news pages, M John Harrison became the first science fiction author to win the Booker Prize, Stacy Keach died at 85, and Paul McCartney became a billionaire.
